body:
Hi, and thanks for actionlint — we run it as a required check on our shared workflows repository, and it has caught real mistakes for us.

GitHub announced a new `uses:` syntax today (2026-07-30) that actionlint doesn't recognise yet:

> [Reference same-repository actions with self-repository syntax](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-07-30-reference-same-repository-actions-with-self-repository-syntax/)
>
> A `uses:` value that starts with `$/` resolves to your workflow's own repository at the exact commit that is running, with no checkout required.

Per the announcement it works "everywhere the workspace-relative `./` syntax works, including workflow steps, composite action steps, nested composition, and reusable workflow calls". It requires runner `2.336.0` or newer and is currently github.com only.

### Current behaviour

With actionlint 1.7.12:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/example.yml
name: Example
on: workflow_dispatch
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: $/.github/actions/my-action
```

```
example.yml:8:15: specifying action "$/.github/actions/my-action" in invalid format because ref is missing. available formats are "{owner}/{repo}@{ref}" or "{owner}/{repo}/{path}@{ref}" [action]
```

### Expected behaviour

`$/<path>` accepted without a `@ref`, since the absence of a ref is precisely the point — the action resolves to the commit already running.

### Why it matters

The syntax exists to remove a real desynchronisation risk. Referencing an action of the same repository as `owner/repo/path@v1` hardcodes a version inside the workflow, so a caller pinning `workflow.yml@v1.5.0` still loads the `@v1` action, and any push before the tag moves leaves a window where a new workflow runs against an older action.

### Workaround in the meantime

For anyone landing here, `-ignore` scoped to this single message keeps the rest of the linting intact:

```bash
actionlint -ignore 'specifying action "\$/.+" in invalid format because ref is missing'
```

Happy to help test a fix if that's useful. Thanks again for the tool.

comments.body:
> For anyone landing here, `-ignore` scoped to this single message keeps the rest of the linting intact:
> 
> actionlint -ignore 'specifying action "\$/.+" in invalid format because ref is missing'

Similarly, the `paths.<path-glob>.ignore` [config setting](https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint/blob/main/docs/config.md):

```yaml
paths:
  .github/workflows/**/*.{yaml,yml}:
    ignore:
      - reusable workflow call "\$/.+" at "uses" is not following the format
      - specifying action "\$/.+" in invalid format because ref is missing
```

_Update:_ Added `ignore` config for `$/` self-reference reusable workflows.

This is needed, when running `zizmor` together with this linter, the linters disagree and zizmor wants `$/` syntax while actions lint does not support it and fails with `specifying action "\$/.+" in invalid format because ref is missing`. This came in https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor/pull/2271.

Confirmed with the current stable 1.7.12 Docker distribution at `rhysd/actionlint@sha256:b1934ee5f1c509618f2508e6eb47ee0d3520686341fec936f3b79331f9315667` during https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/pull/55. Runner 2.338.0 successfully resolves and executes `uses: $/.github/actions/npm-cache`, while actionlint rejects the same reference as missing a ref.

Minimal reproduction:

```yaml
name: Self-reference
on: workflow_dispatch
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: $/.github/actions/npm-cache
```

Run the pinned image against this workflow: the valid reference produces `[action] specifying action ... in invalid format because ref is missing`.

Our temporary workaround uses `paths` to ignore only that exact action reference/diagnostic in its two calling workflow files. A separate contract verifies that the referenced action exists. A real bundled-checker rehearsal confirms a different invalid reference and a genuine ShellCheck SC2086 still fail; no global action/shell rule is disabled. The exception has an explicit removal condition when support ships.

Suggested implementation: recognize `$/<nonempty-relative-path>` as a distinct same-repository reference before remote `owner/repo@ref` validation, preserve validation of malformed/empty paths, and add action/composite/reusable-workflow cases. The downstream reproducible positive/negative experiment is `experiments/issue-54/rehearse-actionlint.py` in the linked PR. No duplicate issue opened because this report already tracks the cause.
This is the hottest issue and I humbly request the owners to merge the PR soon.

For information, there's a fork with this fix and some more additions there :
https://github.com/jdx/jactionlint

> This is the hottest issue and I humbly request the owners to merge the PR soon.

Ping @rhysd for request to merge
The lack of response from maintainer suggests that this project has been abandoned and https://github.com/jdx/jactionlint or https://github.com/kjanat/actionlint should be used instead

Confirmed with the current actionlint 1.7.12 and zizmor 1.32.0 that the local-action spelling conflict remains. Minimal workflow (with an `action.yml` at `.github/actions/setup-node`):
```yaml
name: self action
on: workflow_dispatch
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-node
```
`actionlint -shellcheck= -pyflakes= repro.yml` reports `"$/.github/actions/setup-node" is invalid value for "uses" ... ref is missing` at the local action. zizmor's self-repository guidance prefers the `$/' spelling, while `./.github/actions/setup-node` is accepted by actionlint and requires a narrow self-repository exception in zizmor.

We retain that narrow exception and the conventional `./` syntax; neither analyzer is disabled: https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/pull/103 . Accepting `$/' local-action references, as proposed in #732, would let downstream repositories remove this exception. The fixture and exact latest-version output are preserved in that PR's issue evidence.

Confirmed for reusable workflow calls with released actionlint 1.7.12 and zizmor 1.32.0:

```yaml
jobs:
  security:
    uses: $/.github/workflows/security.yml
```

GitHub accepts this syntax, and zizmor recommends it. actionlint reports `reusable workflow call "$/.github/workflows/security.yml" ... is not following the format ...`. Our temporary wrapper normalizes only valid same-repository workflow filenames to the equivalent `./` form on stdin, preserving the original filename and working directory. actionlint still loads the actual callee and validates inputs; no workflow-call diagnostics are suppressed. Malformed paths are not rewritten. The existing queue validation and supported runner-label configuration remain separate.

PR #732's normalization approach would let us delete this compatibility transformation after a release. Reproduction, passing real actionlint validation, and malformed-path regression are in https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/pull/557 .

title: Support the new `$/` self-repository `uses:` syntax
